claim: Large changes in U.S. bank reserve balances can be driven by Treasury General Account flows even when the Fed securities portfolio is nearly unchanged; therefore Fed asset size alone is an incomplete short-horizon liquidity proxy.
evidence_for: Fed H.4.1 Sep. 10, 2026: Sep. 9 reserve balances $3.0365T, up $107.2B week/week; TGA $843.7B, down $100.7B; securities held outright nearly flat.
practical_implication: Track TGA and reserve balances jointly with Fed assets when assessing short-term dollar liquidity.

claim: With ON RRP usage near zero, Treasury cash rebuilds have less capacity to be absorbed by a decline in ON RRP and may transmit more directly into bank reserves/private liquidity than during the high-ON-RRP regime.
evidence_for: NY Fed source via FRED: ON RRP usage about $5.255B on Sep. 11, 2026.
Treasury Aug. 3 financing estimate assumes $950B end-Sep cash balance versus Fed H.4.1 TGA about $843.7B on Sep. 9.
evidence_against: The exact end-Sep TGA path is not guaranteed and other liability/asset flows can offset reserve effects.
practical_implication: Do not reuse 2021-2024 Treasury-liquidity heuristics without adjusting for the depleted RRP buffer.
